sentences.text: Amphicotylus possessed a roughly triangular, platyrostral skull shape similar to modern crocodilians.
The species is distinguished from Goniopholis by having palatines completely separated by the choana.
Excavations in 1993 at the East Camarasaurus Quarry in Wyoming produced the largest and most complete goniopholidid skeleton known.
The hyoid apparatus morphology suggests A. milesi could raise the ventral fold of the gular valve to separate narial and oral passages, allowing it to open its mouth underwater while breathing.
Edward Drinker Cope described Amphicotylus in 1878 using dorsal and lumbar vertebrae, ribs, and osteoderms.
Cope named the type species A. lucasii after Superintendent Lucas and estimated the animal was smaller than the modern American Alligator.
Phylogenetic studies consistently place Amphicotylus deep within Goniopholididae, just outside the clade containing most European members.
Amphicotylus lived during the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic in Colorado, Wyoming, and Oklahoma.
Amphicotylus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian, between 152.21 and 143.1 million years ago.
There is a debate regarding the relationship of Denazinosuchus to Amphicotylus, with some studies viewing it as a sister taxon and others placing it in the European clade.
